info.title: Corral Dashboard API
info.description: The host-side control plane for Corral: repos, projects, GitHub issues, and the automations engine (actions, hooks, flows, runs, prompts) plus the host-wide logs and trace tree. The dashboard UI is one client; the `corral api` CLI and the host Claude skill are others. Loopback-only and token-gated. Mutating calls (POST/PUT/DELETE) require the operator to enable API writes in global settings; reads are always allowed.

parameters.description: Include this repo's actions plus global ones; omit for global only.

get.summary: Live per-project status — up/down, and the working/waiting activity signal
get.description: The activity field is how you tell whether a project's Claude is actively working ('working') or idle at the prompt waiting on the user ('waiting'), or the container is down ('off'). It's computed from real completion activity (POST /v1/messages when the traffic is decrypted, else a proxy.log heuristic).

put.description: After starting a web app in the sandbox, set the user-facing port to watch (e.g. a docs site on 1313), so the Live View tab opens it without the user hunting for it. Send 0 to clear.

List connected MCP servers with live status
get.description: Drives `claude mcp list` on the host. status is connected | needs_auth | pending | unknown. A read — always allowed.

post.description: Runs `claude mcp add --scope user`. A mutating call — when made by the CLI/host Claude it requires API writes to be enabled; the browser is never gated.

delete.description: Runs `claude mcp remove <name>`. Mutating — gated for the CLI/Claude, never for the browser.

post.summary: Start the interactive OAuth login for an MCP server
post.description: Runs `claude mcp login <name>` in a bridged terminal (the browser attaches over a WebSocket). Use this for a server whose status is needs_auth. Mutating — gated for the CLI/Claude; in practice the user completes the browser OAuth.

put.description: cadenceSeconds is the interval; catchUp fires once on wake when overdue (else the miss is skipped); enabled pauses it. Mutating — gated for CLI/Claude, not the browser. The tick that FIRES a scheduled flow is never gated.

get.summary: Get the global assistant's capability (read-only vs act)
get.description: configured=false means the user hasn't chosen yet → the dashboard shows a first-run prompt. Governs the app-wide chat dock only.

put.description: readonly = look only; act = can run corral api (still fenced by the API-writes gate). A browser preference, not itself gated.
